name: Hourglass-Furnace
geological_features: Twin caldera system connected by lava channel
specific_features: Predictably alternating eruption cycle between twin calderas
description: Hourglass-Furnace is defined by its twin calderas, massive volcanic structures connected by a subterranean lava channel that causes them to erupt in perfect alternation. When one fills and overflows, the pressure shifts to the other, creating a geological timepiece that cycles with metronomic regularity every forty-seven standard hours.

The toxic atmosphere is thick with sulfur compounds and volcanic ash, tinting everything in shades of amber and rust. The heat is relentless, and the ground trembles constantly with the rhythm of the planet's volcanic heartbeat.

Extremophilic microbes thrive in the thermal vents between the twin calderas, feeding on sulfur compounds and mineral-rich superheated water. Their metabolic processes are synchronized to the eruption cycle, suggesting they have evolved to exploit the planet's geological rhythm.

The predictable eruption pattern makes Hourglass-Furnace one of the few volcanic worlds where mining operations can be conducted with reasonable safety margins. The uranium and titanium deposits are substantial, and the geothermal energy potential is virtually limitless for any installation that can withstand the heat.
